passage: Rain drummed on the roof of the crèche, and only a few minutes were left before the parents came. Pankaj wanted Ishita's doll in the yellow dress, and Ishita wanted the red toy truck in Pankaj's hands. Pankaj held the truck out. "You have the truck, I have the doll, then we swap back." Ishita paused, then nodded and put the doll in his arms. Ishita drove the truck under the table with engine noises while Pankaj brushed the doll's hair. When the bell rang for pick-up, they swapped back without being told.

qa.q: What did Pankaj offer to swap for the doll?
qa.a: Pankaj offered the red toy truck.

qa.q: What was Pankaj feeling about the doll before he made his offer?
qa.a: Pankaj wanted a turn with the doll and was hopeful about getting one. The truck was his way of asking for it.

qa.q: What other approach could work if Ishita had said no, and why?
qa.a: They could ask a grown-up for a timer so each gets a turn with each toy. A timer gives a fair count neither has to argue over.

qa.q: How does the swap look to Ishita?
qa.a: Ishita gets the truck that was wanted, so the trade feels fair. Swapping back when the bell rang shows Ishita trusted it.

grounding: A child swaps a toy truck for a turn with the other child's doll so both get something wanted.

passage: On the colony lawn in Chandigarh, Baljeet had the yellow truck and Parul had the doll with the pink dress. Baljeet kept looking at the doll, his chin on his knees. Parul kept looking at the truck, twisting her plait. "Swap?" Baljeet said, holding out the truck. Parul thought, then handed over the doll. "Only till lunch." Baljeet nodded. They played side by side, each with the other's toy.

qa.q: What colour was the doll's dress?
What was Baljeet thinking when he held out the truck?
qa.a: He felt hopeful that Parul wanted the truck as much as he wanted the doll.

qa.q: What else could Baljeet try if Parul said no?
qa.a: He could offer a turn with the truck while asking for a short turn with the doll.

qa.q: How does the swap look to Parul?
qa.a: Parul finds it fair and fun, since she gets the truck she wanted.

grounding: A child swaps his toy truck for a turn with his friend's doll, and both get something they want.

passage:
"Jeevan, can I play with your doll?" Arnab asked.
"No."
"Please?"
"No, she's mine."
Arnab looked at his truck. "If you give me the doll, you can have the truck."
Jeevan stopped. "The whole truck?"
"Till snack time."
"Okay!"
They swapped. Jeevan zoomed the truck, and Arnab combed the doll's hair.

qa.q: Until when did Arnab offer the truck?
What was Jeevan feeling when he said "Okay!"?
qa.a: He was happy and excited to get the truck.

qa.q: What else could Arnab offer next time?
qa.a: Playing together with both toys, so neither has to give one up.

qa.q: How does the swap look to Arnab?
qa.a: Arnab is pleased because his offer worked and he got the doll.

grounding: A child swaps his truck for a turn with a friend's doll, and both get something they want.
